subject: CSV mis-match between micro_global() and ectotherm()

messages.author: 9c7ab3c81d833137
messages.subject: CSV mis-match between micro_global() and ectotherm()
parts:
Hello fellow NicheMappers,

I'm after some advice when running the microclimate model followed by the ectotherm model over a large spatial extent. I'm hitting a few problems and I hope someone can help.

I think I have the first bit (running the microclimate model) pretty much worked out. I've written a loop which will go across my geographical extent and calculate microclimate for each point across my surface. However, an individual point takes upwards of 350KB of RAM to store all the data - over several thousand points, it can very rapidly eat all your available free memory. So I looked into the various arguments for micro_global() and found there's options to writecsv and write_input. If I set these both to '1', I send up with a bunch of CSV files written to disk (as you'd expect). I was hoping I could compute microclimate across my extent, writing CSV files as I go, to reduce the RAM requirements. However, after a fair bit of experimentation, I can't quite figure out how to use these files.

The ectotherm model's documentation says, that, in the absence of a list (micro) containing the microclimate predictions, it will search for the CSVs in a predefined directory. No problem; I've told ectotherm() where it can find these CSVs for a solitary test point. However, there seems to be quite a bit of mis-match between what ectotherm() is asking for and what micro_climate() actually produces. 

For example:

Run micro_global() for a point and set writecsv=1 and write_input=1. This generates 4 CSV files in your working directory (metout, shadmet, shadsoil and soil) plus another 39 CSV files in 'working directory/micro csv input/'.
Run ectotherm(), specifying your working directory with the CSV files and you get the error: 

cannot open file 'f:/scratch/rainfall.csv': No such file or directory

Makes sense - there's definitely no rainfall.csv file in that directory. So I look in ../micro csv input/ but there's no rainfall.csv in there either. There's rain.csv and RAINhr.csv but that's it. I moved rain.csv into the root working directory (thinking that perhaps there's just a small mis-match in names between micro_global() and ectotherm()) and renamed it to rainfall.csv.

I re-run the model and get the error:

cannot open file 'f:/scratch/ectoin.csv': No such file or directory

Here's where I'm really stuck (assuming that renaming rain.csv to rainfall.csv isn't an issue); I have checked both directories and can't see any .csv file close to that name.

I was wondering what the best way to proceed would be? I suppose the easiest solution would be to write a loop which first calculates microclimate for a point, followed by ectotherm() - then saving that output. Would this be the best solution? For example:

test.ecto<-list()
for (i in 1:nrow(test.points)){
  micro<-micro_global(loc=test.points[1,])
  test.ecto[[i]]<-ectotherm()
}

Or would it be best to first calculate microclimate across my entire extent and then run the ectotherm model? If so, could someone suggest how this may be possible, given that the writecsv arguments don't allow you to specify a file path (therefore, I can't give each output a different name or directory location on each iteration of a loop). I think I prefer this second solution because it's easier to write the code to run in parallel when an ordered list of microclimate data can be fed into ectotherm() but, at present, I can't think of a way around this given that the micro_global() CSV outputs don't match and the fact that I can't specify a file name to prevent the output being overwritten on each iteration of a loop..

I hope that all makes sense and sorry for the really long post!

Thanks in advance for any assistance,
Simon

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: CSV mis-match between micro_global() and ectotherm()
parts:
Hello Simon,

When I'm running lots of sites, I just collate what I want to keep as far as outputs per site, together with the coordinates, into a matrix and write it to a csv file using 'write.table' with append = T so all the parallel runs of the model are writing to the same file (for some reason, this seems to work without write permission conflicts):

yearoutput<-cbind(longlat[1],longlat[2],yearout)
write.table(yearoutput, file ="yearoutput.csv", sep = ",", col.names = F, qmethod = "double", append = T)

The 'write_input' option is mainly for me when debugging so I can recreate an R run in the FORTRAN IDE I use. The 'write.csv' option does have some issues and I might just remove it altogether in the next version.

All the best,
Mike

Hi Mike,

May I ask what parallelisation approach you take? My current method (below) fails. I think it's because ectotherm() doesn't know where to find the object 'micro' when running in parallel:

library(NicheMapR)
library(doParallel)

cl<-makeCluster(7)
registerDoParallel(cl)

foreach(i = 1:nrow(caribbean.points), .verbose=F, .packages=c("NicheMapR")) %dopar% {
  
  micro<-micro_global(loc=caribbean.points[i,], nyears=1, timeinterval = 365)
  ecto<-ectotherm()
  yearoutput<-cbind(caribbean.points[1,1],caribbean.points[1,2],ecto$environ)

write.table(yearoutput, file ="yearoutput.csv", sep = ",", col.names = F, qmethod = "double", append = T)
  
}

stopCluster(cl)
end<-Sys.time()
end-start



Error in { : task 1 failed - "object 'micro' not found"

It seems like the object 'micro', once calculated, isn't passed to ectotherm(). If I change %dopar% to %do% (such that it runs sequentially) I have no problems, apart from it being slow compared to a parallel run.

All the best,
Simon

messages.author: e46cb5dd353b7dfb
messages.subject: Re: CSV mis-match between micro_global() and ectotherm()
parts:
Hi Sean,

This should work:

library(doParallel)
library(NicheMapR)

caribbean.points<- matrix(data = c(rep(140, 3), rep(-35, 3)), nrow = 3, ncol = 2)

cl<-makeCluster(3)
registerDoParallel(cl)
foreach(i = 1:nrow(caribbean.points), .verbose=F, .packages=c("NicheMapR")) %dopar% {

micro = micro_global(loc=caribbean.points[i,], nyears=1, timeinterval = 12)
 
  nyears = micro$nyears
  maxshades = micro$MAXSHADES
  REFL = micro$REFL
  DEP = micro$DEP
  metout = micro$metout
  shadmet = micro$shadmet
  soil = micro$soil
  shadsoil = micro$shadsoil
  soilmoist = micro$soilmoist
  shadmoist = micro$shadmoist
  humid = micro$humid
  shadhumid = micro$shadhumid
  soilpot = micro$soilpot
  shadpot = micro$shadpot
  RAINFALL = micro$RAINFALL
  ectoin = rbind(as.numeric(micro$ALTT), as.numeric(micro$REFL)[1],
    micro$longlat[1], micro$longlat[2])


  ecto<-ectotherm(nyears = nyears, REFL = REFL, DEP = DEP, maxshades = maxshades,
    metout = metout, shadmet = shadmet, soil = soil, shadsoil = shadsoil,
    soilmoist = soilmoist, shadmoist = shadmoist, humid = humid, shadhumid = shadhumid,
    soilpot = soilpot, shadpot = shadpot, RAINFALL = RAINFALL, ectoin = ectoin)

yearoutput<-cbind(caribbean.points[1,1],caribbean.points[1,2],ecto$environ)
  write.table(yearoutput, file ="yearoutput.csv", sep = ",", col.names = F, qmethod = "double", append = T)

}

stopCluster(cl)

All the best,
Mike
